[[Category:English terms with audio pronunciation|HEY]] * Rhymes: [[Rhymes:English/eɪ|-eɪ]][[Category:Rhymes:English/eɪ|HEY]][[Category:Rhymes:English/eɪ/1 syllable|HEY]] * [[Appendix:Glossary#homophone|Homophones]]: [[:hay#English|hay]]; [[:hae#English|hae]] ([[w:Pane–pain merger|pane–pain merger]])[[Category:English terms with homophones|HEY]] ===Etymology 1=== From [[w:Middle English|Middle English]][[Category:English terms inherited from Middle English|HEY]][[Category:English terms derived from Middle English|HEY]] [[:hey#Middle_English|hey]], [[:hei#Middle_English|hei]], also without ''h-'' in [[:ey#Middle_English|ey]], from [[w:Old English|Old English]][[Category:English terms inherited from Old English|HEY]][[Category:English terms derived from Old English|HEY]] [[:Reconstruction:Old English/he|*hē]], [[:ea#Old_English|ēa]] (interjection), attested as first element in [[:hela#Old_English|hēlā]], [[:eala#Old_English|ēalā]] (“O!, alas!, oh!, lo!”). Cognate with [[w:Dutch language|Dutch]] [[:hé#Dutch|hé]], [[:hei#Dutch|hei]] (“hi, hey”), [[w:German language|German]] [[:hei#German|hei]] (“hey, wow”), [[w:Danish language|Danish]] and [[w:Swedish language|Swedish]] [[:hej#Swedish|hej]] (“hello, hey”), [[w:Faroese language|Faroese]] [[:hey#Faroese|hey]] (“hey, hello”), [[w:Old Norse|Old Norse]], [[w:Icelandic language|Icelandic]] and [[w:Norwegian language|Norwegian]] [[:hei#Norwegian|hei]] (“hey”), [[w:Polish language|Polish]] [[:hej#Polish|hej]] (“hey, hello”), [[w:Romanian language|Romanian]] [[:hei#Romanian|hei]], [[w:Russian language|Russian]] [[:эй#Russian|эй]] (ej, “hey”); see [[:heigh#English|heigh]]. Probably a natural[[Category:English sound-symbolic terms|HEY]] expression, as may be inferred from its presence with similar meaning in many other unrelated languages: for example, [[w:Burmese language|Burmese]] [[:ဟေး#Burmese|ဟေး]] (he:), [[w:Finnish language|Finnish]] [[:hei#Finnish|hei]], Unami ''hè'', and [[w:Mandarin Chinese|Mandarin]] [[:哎#Mandarin|哎]] (āi)[[Category:Mandarin terms with redundant transliterations|HEY]], and various sound-alikes as [[w:Ancient Greek|Ancient Greek]] [[:εἶα#Ancient_Greek|εἶα]] (eîa) and [[w:Latin|Latin]] [[:eia#Latin|eia]], [[:eho#Latin|eho]], [[w:Sanskrit|Sanskrit]] [[:हे#Sanskrit|हे]] (he). See also [[:hello#English|hello]]. ====Alternative forms==== * [[:hay#English|hay]] * [[:heigh#English|heigh]] ====Interjection==== hey[[Category:English lemmas|HEY]][[Category:English interjections|HEY]][[Category:English entries with incorrect language header|HEY]][[Category:Pages with entries|HEY]][[Category:Pages with 9 entries|HEY]] ([[Appendix:Glossary#informal|informal]][[Category:English informal terms|HEY]]) # An [[exclamation]] to get [[attention]]. #:
'''Hey''', look at this!
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] #:
'''Hey'''! Listen!
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] # A [[protest]] or [[reprimand]]. #:
'''Hey'''! Stop that!
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] # An [[expression]] of [[surprise]]. #:
'''Hey'''! This is new!
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] # An [[:informal#English|informal]] [[:greeting#English|greeting]], similar to [[:hi#English|hi]]. #:
'''Hey'''! How's it going?
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] # A [[request]] for [[repetition]] or [[explanation]]; an expression of [[confusion]]. #:
'''Hey'''? [[:how's that#English|How's that]]?
[[Category:English terms with usage examples|HEY]] # Used as a [[:tag question#English|tag question]], to emphasise what goes before or to request that the listener express an opinion about what has been said. #*
'''1900''', [[:w:Joseph Conrad|Joseph Conrad]], [[:w:Lord Jim|Lord Jim]], page vi. 54:[[Category:English terms with quotations|HEY]]
"Who 's a cur - now - '''hey'''?"
[[Category:English terms with quotations|HEY]]
# A meaningless [[beat]] [[marker]] or extra, [[filler]] [[syllable]] in song lyrics. #:
The chorus is "nana na na, nana na na '''hey hey hey''', goodbye".
